title: Equations and valid reasoning
purpose: Build a reliable method for changing an equation without silently changing its solution set.

lessons.title: Linear equations and formula rearrangement
lessons.objective: Isolate a specified variable, state any divisor restrictions, and verify a proposed solution by substitution.
lessons.coverage: Balance operations, distributive signs, equations with fractions, identity versus contradiction, and rearranging a formula with several symbols.
lessons.activity: A step checker shows two sides of an equation. Predict whether an operation preserves the solution set, apply it, and explain an invalid division by a possible zero.
families: Construct linear equations from a known rational solution, including all-real and no-solution cases
Choose or complete a valid symbolic rearrangement with required parameter restrictions
lessons.generatorRules: Use small integers and rational coefficients. Deliberately label separate unique, identity, and contradiction families. Do not accidentally divide by a zero coefficient.
lessons.commonError: Changing only one side, distributing a minus incorrectly, or dividing by a parameter without checking zero.
lessons.feedback: Highlight the first operation that changes equivalence; route sign errors to b01 and distribution errors to b03.
lessons.checkpoint: One numerical equation, one formula rearrangement, one identity/contradiction classification, and one invalid-step explanation.

lessons.title: Inequalities and absolute value
lessons.objective: Express the full solution set of a linear, compound, or absolute-value inequality with correct endpoints.
lessons.coverage: Sign reversal after multiplying by a negative, interval and set notation, unions versus intersections, and distance interpretations of absolute value.
lessons.activity: Predict an interval, enter its endpoints and inclusion flags, and compare its number-line representation with test values on either side of a boundary.
families: Generate a linear or compound inequality from a known interval
Translate an absolute-value tolerance condition into an interval or union and back
lessons.generatorRules: Include strict and inclusive boundaries, negative multipliers, empty sets, and all-real cases. Infinity is never an included endpoint.
lessons.commonError: Keeping the inequality direction after division by a negative, using AND where OR is needed, or including an open endpoint.
lessons.feedback: Test a counterexample near the incorrect endpoint and reconnect absolute value with distance.
lessons.checkpoint: A negative-coefficient inequality, a compound interval, an absolute-value case, and a tolerance interpretation.

lessons.title: Quadratics and complex roots
lessons.objective: Choose a quadratic solution method, return every root in the requested number system, and verify the roots.
lessons.coverage: Factoring, square-root method, completing the square, quadratic formula, discriminant, repeated roots, i notation, and conjugate pairs.
lessons.activity: Compare a parabola's real intercepts with an exact root list. Change the discriminant and explain why an empty real-root list can coexist with complex roots.
families: Construct quadratics with two real roots, a repeated root, or a complex conjugate pair
Select the most direct method and identify an omitted plus-or-minus branch
lessons.generatorRules: Specify real or complex answers. Include rational and simple radical roots. Preserve multiplicity in a separate field when requested; do not confuse roots with x-intercepts.
lessons.commonError: Dropping one square-root branch, treating sqrt(a+b) as sqrt(a)+sqrt(b), or reporting a complex root as a real intercept.
lessons.feedback: Substitute both candidate roots and use the discriminant to classify the expected answer before recomputing.
lessons.checkpoint: Factorable, completing-square, nonreal-root, and discriminant interpretation items.

lessons.title: Restrictions and extraneous solutions
lessons.objective: Solve rational and radical equations while preserving original restrictions and rejecting invalid candidate roots.
lessons.coverage: Original denominator exclusions, even-root domains, clearing denominators, squaring as a one-way implication, and checking candidates in the original equation.
lessons.activity: Sort generated candidates into valid, excluded, and extraneous categories, then show which original condition rejects each one.
families: Solve rational equations whose clearing step creates an excluded candidate
Solve radical equations whose squaring step creates an extraneous candidate
lessons.generatorRules: Generate from factored forms and verify every candidate against the original expression. Include zero, one, and two valid-root cases with explicit real domains.
lessons.commonError: Accepting every root of the transformed equation or erasing a denominator restriction after cancellation.
lessons.feedback: Show the original expression at the rejected candidate, then link b04 if the restriction was lost while simplifying.
lessons.checkpoint: A rational equation, a radical equation, a complete restriction list, and an explanation of why squaring needs a check.

anchor.prompt: Solve sqrt(x+6)=x over the real numbers.
anchor.answer: x=3. Squaring produces candidates 3 and -2, but x must be nonnegative. The candidate -2 fails the original equation.

moduleExit: Use the eight-item module blueprint, with two items per lesson. A restriction or extraneous-root error must receive targeted remediation even when the overall score is high.
